key_insight: SAGE-PINN embeds axisymmetric cylindrical geometry and conservation laws directly into the network to remove singularity issues at the axis while learning coupled flow and heat transfer without labeled data.
engineering_relevance: It offers a mesh-free way to simulate stenosed-artery nanofluid flow and thermal transport in cylindrical geometries, which is useful for biomedical and multiphysics design studies.
method: Uses the parity-preserving variable s = r^2 and a modified stream-function form to eliminate explicit 1/r singular terms.
Enforces boundary conditions analytically with boundary-fitted ansätze so constraints are satisfied exactly.
Stabilizes training with staged momentum-thermal-joint optimization, residual normalization, parameter continuation, and a drift guard.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions, achieving single-precision mass conservation and central-range errors of about 1.6% for axial velocity and 9.1% for temperature.
watch_item: Performance degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-influenced slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer, so careful continuation and tuning may still be needed.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
